problem: The product tried to do too many things and users were interested in one.
title: Burbn's founders cut features and rebuild the app around photo sharing
context: Burbn was a location check-in app with many features, and the founders noticed that people mostly used its photo features.
decision_made: Remove other planned features, rebuild around photo sharing and rename the app Instagram.
action_taken: Launched on the Apple App Store on 6 October 2010.
observed_outcome: Reports say about 25,000 users on day one, 100,000 downloads in the first week and about one million users by mid-December 2010.
lessons: Following what users actually do, and cutting everything else, can reveal a stronger product.
limitations: Sources are mostly secondary and the first-day figure is sometimes described as uploads rather than users. Survivorship bias applies, since many pivots fail.

claims.claim_text: The founders cut Burbn's other features and rebuilt the app around photo sharing as Instagram.
Instagram reached about one million users within roughly two months of its October 2010 launch.
